evidence: Plaut. Ps. 1052: Hahae, nunc dēmum mī animus in tūtō est locō
terms.comment: Lewis & Short (s.v. ha): “an exclamation of joy, thank heavens!”. Traupman gives ehem! for a phew of glad surprise or relief (p. 359).

terms.grammar: perfect of respīrō; the present respīrō too
terms.comment: Cicero’s word in the letters for relief after worry.
The words of relief after a fright.

phrases.latin: Hahae, nunc dēmum mī animus in tūtō est locō
phrases.english: Phew, now at last my mind is in a safe place

phrases.latin: Hahahae, requiēvī, quia intrō abiit odium meum.
phrases.english: Phew, I can rest, now that my pest has gone in.

phrases.latin: accēpī litterās tuās et paulum respīrāvī
phrases.english: I got your letter and breathed a little more freely

phrases.latin: Dī mē servant, salva rēs est.
phrases.english: The gods are keeping me; all’s well.

re-short.html: The lexicon’s ruling on re- before sc, sp, st (Bennett §48 rejects the lengthening for the lost d of red-). Still under Jack’s review.

sources: Lewis & Short: ha (hahae) · Lewis & Short: respiro · Lewis & Short: salvus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 359.
